title: Investigate erroneous token delta across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private metering pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported billing deltas and unexpected token consumption spikes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Initial symptoms: short-duration bursts of 30-60% higher token counts for identical requests, intermittent in time and across tenants. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, short-term mitigation (customer credits + ingestion filter), and long-term pipeline fixes (idempotent ingestion, stronger dedup keys, reconciliation jobs).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use canonical prompt set from customer QA suite (10k tokens total across 1k requests).
2) Send requests through hosted API behind our edge proxies with intermittent simulated network flaps (drop 0.5% of ACKs).
3) Observe metering stream and aggregated token count in billing pipeline (compare runtime token emission vs aggregated meter).
4) Repeat test against Dedicated cluster and a Private VPC deployment with the same agent telemetry config.
observed_behavior: Aggregated billing records show duplicate token accounting in 0.8-1.6% of requests during brief network disturbances. For one affected customer, a 72-hour window produced a +14k token delta (~$420) compared to runtime logs. Duplicates correlate with repeated ingestion events that share the same request_id but different sequence checksums.
expected_behavior: Token accounting should be idempotent: for a given request_id and final sequence checksum, the billing pipeline should accept only a single token emission. Hosted/Dedicated/Private telemetry should use unified deduplication semantics so identical client behavior yields identical billed tokens.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-14 09:10 UTC: Customer support opened escalation (QuickCart Inc.) — reported 12% higher invoice for December usage; provided sample request IDs.

2025-02-14 11:00 UTC: Correlated sample request IDs with runtime logs — the serving runtime shows a single generation, but the ingestion stream contains two events separated by ~2s with identical request_id and different partial_checksums.

2025-02-15 14:22 UTC: Instrumented edge proxy to log ACKs and retransmits; found that when ACK not received by proxy due to transient connection reset, proxy retried forwarding the telemetry event with same request_id but omitted the final_checksum header (older client shard).

2025-02-16 08:30 UTC: Reproduced locally by dropping telemetry ACKs — ingestion accepted both events because dedup key used (request_id + final_checksum) and second event had missing final_checksum, generating a null value that bypassed dedup check.

2025-02-17 16:00 UTC: Dedicated cluster telemetry agent (v2.3.0) hashes account_id differently (org_id vs customer_id) causing reconciliation mismatch between runtime and billing aggregation for Private deployments.

2025-02-18 10:00 UTC: Evaluated effect size across fleet — ~0.5% overall duplicate ingestion, but concentrated on customers with older telemetry agents and high request rates; estimated refund exposure ~$25k/month if unmitigated.
root_cause: Telemetry ingestion lacked strict idempotency: deduplication relied on request_id + final_checksum. Edge proxies and older telemetry agents sometimes forwarded events without final_checksum or with variant account identifiers, which produced distinct dedup keys and allowed duplicate acceptance. Additionally, Private deployments had agent-level identifier mismatches (account_id vs org_id) leading to aggregation mis-attribution during reconciliation.
short_term_mitigation: Deploy ingestion filter v1.1 to drop duplicate events when request_id matches a recently-seen request within a 5-minute window regardless of checksum (hotfix).
Issue one-time credits to impacted customers (QuickCart Inc. credited $500) pending complete reconciliation.
Enable verbose telemetry sampling for affected customers to collect full event bodies for backfill verification.
Patch edge proxy config to hold for 250ms for ACK confirmation before retrying telemetry forwarding (config change rolled to Hosted and Dedicated).
Communicate incident summary and expected remediation timeline to customers and Sales/CS owners.
long_term_fix_plan: Make ingestion idempotent using a canonical dedup key: canonical_request_id = sha256(request_id + canonical_checksum + normalized_account_id).
Upgrade telemetry SDK on Dedicated and Private agents to emit canonical_checksum (final tokenized digest) and normalized_account_id (org_id fallback).
Add a reconciliation batch job (daily) that compares runtime token emission logs to billing aggregates and auto-generates corrective adjustments and invoices flags.
Integrate a chaos test in CI that simulates ACK loss and verifies ingestion dedup behavior end-to-end.
Create migration/backfill job to dedupe the last 90 days of telemetry and produce refund/credit candidates.
qa_and_rollout_plan: Run end-to-end canary against small set of customers (internal + 3 external customers) for 48 hours.
Validate canary by comparing runtime token logs vs ingestion aggregates with tolerances <0.01% duplicates.
If canary passes, progressively roll ingestion filter to 50%/100% across regions within 24 hours.
Schedule telemetry SDK upgrade window for Dedicated and Private customers with clear migration notes and opt-in flags for early adopters.
communication: 2025-02-15: Initial triage email to affected customers acknowledging the billing delta and offering immediate credit options.
2025-02-18: Follow-up with QuickCart Inc. including preliminary root-cause, hotfix applied, and proposed full reconciliation timeline (2 weeks).
Draft public postmortem to be published after remediation and review (target date: 2025-03-07).
